screening_results.reason: Excluded: the paper is a non-empirical clinical imaging review (E1) and does not include a healthy adult sample (E2). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET) not met, I2 (problem-solving task) not met, I3 (healthy adults) not met, I4 (task-related brain activation results) not met. The abstract describes thoracic tumor imaging modalities rather than an experimental fMRI/PET study of problem solving in healthy adults.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving in 13 healthy adult subjects and reports task-related brain activation differences between trained and untrained problems. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

E2: Study involves infant EEG cortical-source localization, not adult participants. Does not use task-based fMRI or PET, nor investigate problem-solving in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria I1-I4 are not met or not demonstrated (no fMRI/PET, no adult problem-solving task, no healthy adult sample, no relevant task-related activation for the review question).

Excluded: E1 (non-empirical review of cervical imaging) and E2 (no healthy adult sample). No inclusion criteria are met or demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (does not involve a problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult participants reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

No evidence the study examines problem-solving or reasoning tasks. Exclusion IDs met: None. Inclusion IDs met: None. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET), I2 (participants performing problem-solving), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (task-related activation). This is a methods-development fMRI QSM paper, not a task-based problem-solving study.

Task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants reporting task-related neural activation. Abstract lacks clear evidence that the scanned task is a problem-solving/reasoning task (n-back working-memory may not meet 'problem solving' definition), so include for full-text review to verify I2.

E2 met: study uses rat PET data (no human participants/healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based human fMRI/PET study), I2 (no humans performing problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). Exclude based on absence of human healthy adult task-based data.

E1 met: the paper is a quantitative meta-analysis of fMRI studies (no original human data). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (reports task-related brain activation results via meta-analysis). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no original human participants performing tasks reported), I3 (no original healthy adult sample reported). Excluded based on abstract indicating synthesis rather than original empirical human data.

Excluded because this is a non-empirical review of posttreatment imaging (E1) and does not include any healthy adult sample (E2). No inclusion criteria are met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adults), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported).

This is a task-based fMRI study using the PASAT (an arithmetic/problem-solving task) in 10 normal subjects with reported task-related brain activations, so it meets I1–I4 and is relevant to problem solving in healthy adults.

E1 applies: this article is a meta-analysis (ALE) and does not present original human participant data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no original human participants performing problem-solving/reasoning tasks reported), I3 (no original healthy adult sample reported), I4 (no primary task-related activation results; only meta-analytic summaries).

Exclusion criteria met: E1 (non-empirical introduction/special-section overview) and E2 (no original healthy adult sample reported). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no participants performing a problem-solving task reported), I3 (no healthy adult sample reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). The abstract describes other empirical papers but contains no original human neuroimaging data.

Abstract describes a theoretical cognitive neuroarchitecture and comparison with brain activation findings but does not report whether this paper contains original task-based fMRI/PET data, participant samples, or task procedures. Insufficient information to confirm I1–I4 from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study of abstract reasoning/problem-solving in alcohol-dependent subjects; reports task-related fMRI investigation. Abstract does not state whether a healthy adult control group is included, so inclusion criterion I3 is not demonstrated. Full-text review needed to confirm presence of healthy adults.

E1 met: this is a meta-analysis/review of PET/fMRI emotion studies and not an original empirical study with new human data. Inclusion criteria: none met. Specifically, I1 not met (not an original task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 not met (does not study problem-solving/reasoning; focuses on emotion), I3 not met (does not include an original healthy adult sample), I4 not met (no original task-related activation results).

Excluded (E2): participants are described as presurgical/implanted (ECoG), indicating clinical patients; no healthy adult sample is reported. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (mental calculation task), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I3 (healthy adults not included or demonstrated).

E2: No healthy adult sample (participants are adolescents/children). Meets I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related activation). Does not meet I3 (no healthy adult group) and I2 is not demonstrated as a problem-solving/reasoning task (navigational memory in youth). Excluded based on absence of healthy adult sample and non-matching task domain.
EXCLUDED because the tasks are motor imagery and passive shoulder motion, not problem-solving/reasoning (I2 not met). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion met: none (E1 and E2 not applicable).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I2 (participants performing a problem-solving or reasoning task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy adult group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E2 not met).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which human volunteers (n=12) performed relational reasoning/problem-solving and maintenance tasks; reports task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study (RPM) with 79 healthy adult participants performing a problem-solving/reasoning task; reports task-related functional network activation and connectivity results. Meets I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related brain activations during chess analysis versus a control spatial task (problem-solving). Human participants performed a reasoning/problem-solving task. Abstract does not explicitly state participant health/age, so inclusion of healthy adult group is unclear; include for full-text review to confirm.

Study uses task-based fMRI in human subjects and reports task-related activation, but the task is a working memory task rather than a problem-solving or reasoning task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 (problem-solving or reasoning task).

Exclusion criteria met: E1 (non-empirical review without original human data) and E2 (no healthy adult sample). No inclusion criteria are met. Specifically, I1 (task-based fMRI or PET study) not demonstrated; I2 (human participants performing a problem-solving task) not demonstrated; I3 (includes healthy adults) not demonstrated; I4 (reports task-related brain activation) not demonstrated.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1), participants performed a reasoning/problem-solving task (RSPM) (I2), includes a healthy adult control group (non-autistic participants) (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication) in human participants, reports task-related parietal activations, and includes healthy adult participants; meets all inclusion criteria (I1–I4). No exclusion criteria met.

E1 met: this is a quantitative meta-analysis (no original human experimental data). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (reports task-related brain activation findings). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (does not examine problem-solving/reasoning tasks; focuses on deception), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly demonstrated in the abstract).

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI study of deductive reasoning (a problem-solving task) in adult humans, describing task-related brain activation across reasoning phases. It therefore meets I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion criteria met: E1 (this is a coordinate-based meta-analysis, not original empirical human data) and E2 (focuses on children; no healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (investigates number processing/calculation in children rather than adult problem-solving), I3 (no healthy adult participants), I4 (reports meta-analytic activation across child studies, not original task-related activation in healthy adults).

E1 met: article is a theoretical/discussion paper (non-empirical review) rather than an original human fMRI/PET study. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related activation).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI, participants (including healthy adults) performed calculation/problem-solving tasks, and task-related brain activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using mental Porteus mazes (problem-solving) in normal subjects and patients, reporting PFC activation results. This satisfies I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — participants performed verbal working memory tasks, not problem-solving or reasoning tasks as required for the review.

Abstract reports an event-related task-based fMRI study of verbal insight/problem-solving (solving Chinese riddles) and reports task-related activations. Participant health/age is not specified, so I3 (healthy adults) is unclear; include for full-text review to confirm.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in humans solving the Wason selection (deductive reasoning) task, with healthy adult participants and reported task-related brain activations. No exclusion criteria apply.

Title/abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study of problem-solving in humans, fulfilling I1 and I2. The abstract does not specify whether a healthy adult group was included (I3) or explicitly report task-related activation results (I4). Insufficient information to confirm I3/I4, so include for full-text review.

Abstract does not specify that this is task-based fMRI or PET, the ages of participants (adult vs. pediatric survivors) are unclear, and task-related activation results are not reported. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the abstract, include for full-text review to determine I1–I4.

Included for full-text review: the abstract describes a task-based fMRI study and includes a healthy comparison group (I1, I3). However, the abstract does not specify that participants performed a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not demonstrated) and does not explicitly report task-related activation results (I4 unclear). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related ventral striatal BOLD prediction-error correlations with fluid IQ. Abstract does not clearly state that the task is a problem-solving/reasoning task (probabilistic reversal learning may not meet I2) nor explicitly confirm a healthy adult sample (I3). Include for full-text review to verify I2 and I3.

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI study of problem solving (Japanese riddles) in human participants and reports task-related brain activations (right hippocampus and cortex). The abstract does not explicitly state the health status or age of participants, so inclusion of healthy adults is not confirmed from abstract alone; include for full-text review to verify I3.

Task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning in human adults reporting task-related brain activation across problem-solving phases; meets all inclusion criteria (I1-I4) and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of analogy generation (a reasoning/problem-solving task) in human participants, reports task-related activation in left frontopolar cortex, and presumably includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of a problem-solving (Tower of London) task with reported task-related brain activation. It does not explicitly state participant health status, so include for full-text review to confirm presence of healthy adult sample.

All inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI study (I1) of humans performing a problem-solving/reasoning task (modified Raven's Matrices) (I2), includes matched healthy adult controls (I3), and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results (I4). No exclusion criteria apply.

fMRI study of surgery residents performing mental rotation (a visual-spatial reasoning/problem-solving task) reporting cortical activation patterns. Participants are human adults (surgery residents) and task-related brain activation is reported, meeting inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Task-based fMRI study of arithmetic word problem solving reporting neural activation. Abstract explicitly confirms task-based fMRI (I1), problem-solving task (I2), and task-related brain activation results (I4). The abstract does not explicitly state the sample are healthy adults, so I3 is unclear; include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

This is a methodological paper on power/sample-size estimation for neuroimaging; it does not report a task-based fMRI or PET study of problem solving in healthy adults. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET) not demonstrated, I2 (problem-solving task) not met, I3 (healthy adult sample) not demonstrated, I4 (task-related activation results) not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are clearly met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study during a mental calculation (problem-solving) task in adult twin pairs, includes task-related brain activation results, and involves adult participants with no pathology reported; thus it meets inclusion criteria I1–I4.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study where human participants performed legal/logical reasoning tasks, and task-related brain activation results are reported. No clinical or non-healthy sample is indicated in the abstract. Thus it meets I1,I2,I3,I4 and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy adult controls), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion ID not met: I2 (does not use a problem-solving or reasoning task; it examines working memory impairment). Therefore excluded for not meeting I2.

Study uses task-based BOLD fMRI, includes healthy control adults, and reports cerebral activation. The abstract describes working memory tasks but does not clearly state participants performed a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 uncertain). Exclusion criteria are not met, so include for full-text review.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review's modality or task requirements. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI or PET; uses diffuse optical tomography), I2 (not a problem-solving/reasoning task; resting-state), I3 (healthy adult sample not demonstrated), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Task-based event-related fMRI study in human subjects performing an arithmetic reasoning/problem-solving task; reports task-related brain activations. No exclusion criteria met; includes healthy adult participants as described.

E1 (non-empirical review) and E2 (no healthy adult sample) apply. No inclusion criteria are met: I1 not met (not a task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 not met (no problem-solving task), I3 not met (pediatric patients, not healthy adults), I4 not met (no task-related activation reported).

Excluded due to E2: single-case patient (Fahr's disease) with no healthy adult sample. Inclusion met: I2 (patient performed numerical/problem-solving tasks). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study—PET was resting/metabolic), I3 (no healthy adults), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

The abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of healthy adult students performing mental calculation (a problem-solving task) and reports task-related brain activation (left angular gyrus). It therefore meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4.

Task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (exact/approximate calculation and magnitude comparison), includes a healthy adult group (20 adults), and reports task-related brain activation results, satisfying all inclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI (I1), reports task-related brain activation (I4), and includes a healthy adult control group (I3). It is unclear whether the PASAT qualifies as a ‘problem-solving or reasoning’ task per I2 (it is a working-memory/mental arithmetic task), so inclusion is uncertain; include for full-text review to resolve I2.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of strategic reasoning (beauty contest), and reports task-related neural activity in medial prefrontal cortex. The abstract does not specify that participants were healthy adults, so full-text review is needed to confirm I3.

E2 met: study includes only 6-7-year-old children (no healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I2 (tasks are number comparison/physical Stroop, not clearly problem-solving/reasoning as required), I3 (no healthy adult group).

Exclusion E2 met: participants are children (ages 8–10) with no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (number-line/arithmetical tasks), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion I3 not met.

E: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participants performed a problem-solving or reasoning task—abstract describes a semantic retrieval task, not problem solving/reasoning) and I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly specified). Therefore exclude based on I2 not met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI and task-related activations (I1, I4) but the tasks are visual search, music, and autobiographic memory—not problem-solving or reasoning (I2 not met). Participant health status is not explicitly stated (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Study uses task-based fMRI and reports task-related activation for a reasoning task (I1,I2,I4), but participants are school-age children (9–14) with no healthy adult sample, so it fails I3 and meets exclusion E2.

Task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants and task-related brain activation results are reported. However, the tasks involve nonsymbolic numerical/spatial processing rather than explicit problem-solving or reasoning, so inclusion status is uncertain—include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related activations during reasoning and episodic memory-based reasoning tasks (meets I1, I2, I4). Abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults, so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where participants performed moral reasoning (a reasoning task), includes a healthy adult control group, and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports task-based PET and fMRI imaging and describes task-related activations during mental navigation/route-memory tasks, but it does not clearly state that the tasks are problem-solving/reasoning nor that participants were healthy adults; possibly a review. Unclear inclusion status, so include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI protocol capturing mental calculation and other cognitive tasks but does not clearly state participants are healthy adults or that problem-solving/reasoning tasks (beyond 'mental calculation') and explicit task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm I2–I4, so include for full-text review.

Exclusion E2 met: study uses task-based fMRI with patients with disorders of consciousness and does not report a healthy adult sample. Inclusion I1 met (task-based fMRI). Inclusion I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task) is not met; Inclusion I3 (healthy adults) is not met; Inclusion I4 (clear report of task-related activation results) is not demonstrated in abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy adult controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — tasks are attention (PASAT) and memory/recall, not clearly problem-solving or reasoning tasks required by the review, so exclude.

Study uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports activations (I1, I3, I4 met) but investigates imagined posture/locomotion, not a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria apply (E1, E2 not met).

The study uses a spatial memory/navigation task (subliminal priming recognition of landmarks and route direction), not a problem-solving or reasoning task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related activations during autobiographical reasoning (a form of reasoning), so I1, I2, and I4 are met. The abstract does not specify participant health/age (I3 unclear). Include for full-text review to confirm healthy adult sample.

Abstract reports a study of numerical inductive reasoning and age-related brain activity in elderly adults, implying human healthy adult participants and task-related brain activation. However, the abstract does not specify the imaging modality (fMRI or PET), so include for full-text review to confirm I1.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of subjects performing a logical deduction/problem-solving task, describes task-related brain activation results, and implies healthy adult participants (no patient sample mentioned). Therefore inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI experiment (I1) with neurologically normal participants performing social and mechanical reasoning tasks (I2) and describes task-related activation/deactivation results (I4). Participant age not explicitly stated as adults, so I3 (healthy adults) is not fully confirmed; include for full-text review to verify age/health status.

Task-based PET study of a problem-solving task (modified Tower of London) including healthy adult controls and reporting task-related cerebral blood flow/activation changes over learning; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded (E2): participants are neurosurgical patients (no healthy adult sample). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task) and I3 (includes healthy adults).

E2: Abstract reports a single patient case and does not mention any healthy adult participants. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI reported), I2 (human participant performed arithmetic/problem-solving), I4 (task-related brain activation results reported). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I3 (no healthy adult sample described).

Task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants and task-related activation are reported (I1, I3, I4). It is unclear from the abstract whether pantomiming unfamiliar tools constitutes a problem-solving/reasoning task (I2 ambiguous—title suggests mechanical problem solving but abstract emphasizes action semantics), so include for full-text review.

E2: Sample consists of high school seniors (adolescents), not clearly a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed arithmetic problem-solving), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no healthy adult group reported).

E2 met: study reports a single PD patient, no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study; FDG-PET was used for resting glucose metabolism), I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adults), I4 (no task-related activation results). No inclusion criteria are satisfied.

Excluded because participants were adolescents (mean age 16.8), so the study does not include a healthy adult sample (E2). The study is task-based fMRI (I1), uses a problem-solving task (Tower of London) (I2), and reports task-related brain activation (I4). Inclusion criterion I3 (healthy adults) is not met.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD contrasts during a problem-solving (insight into Chinese logogriphs) task, so I1, I2, and I4 are clearly met. The abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy adults (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of algebraic problem solving in human participants, reports task-related brain activation, and implies healthy adult participants; meets all inclusion criteria (I1–I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study using a mental arithmetic (problem-solving) task in healthy adult participants, reporting task-related brain activation. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based rtfMRI/EEG neurofeedback), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related BOLD and EEG results). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — participants performed an emotion-induction/self-regulation neurofeedback task, not a problem-solving or reasoning task; therefore excluded.

Excluded because the sample are children (previously institutionalized and comparison children), so there is no healthy adult sample (E2). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not a problem-solving/reasoning task; emotional face Go/Nogo) and I3 (no healthy adult participants).

Excluded due to E2: sample consists of 8-19 year olds (no healthy adult group). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed visuospatial reasoning tasks), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample).

EXCLUDED because E2 is met: the study reports data only from aMCI participants and does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (tasks are visual working memory, not problem-solving/reasoning) and I3 (no healthy adult group).

Abstract describes an event-related fMRI study of a verbal reasoning/problem-solving task and reports task-related brain activation, satisfying I1, I2, and I4. It does not explicitly state inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I2 (task involves problem-solving or reasoning) is not met: the study investigates spatial sequence learning (Corsi block and walking Corsi) rather than a problem-solving/reasoning task. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult participants implied), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (E1, E2).

Abstract reports task-based BOLD fMRI contrasts during a problem-solving (Chinese logogriphs/riddles) task and presents task-related brain activations. It does not explicitly state the participant health status (healthy adults not confirmed), so inclusion criterion I3 is uncertain; include for full-text review to verify participant sample.

Task-based fMRI study using a virtual maze (I1) with healthy adult participants aged 40–55 (I3) and reports neural correlates measured with fMRI (I4). The abstract does not clearly state whether the virtual maze task meets the review’s ‘problem-solving/reasoning’ definition (I2 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (subtraction, multiplication) and finger discrimination in adult participants; reports task-related brain activation (hIPS, PSPL) and conjunction/voxelwise analyses. All inclusion criteria met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI (reversal learning) and PET were used in healthy adults and the abstract reports task-related BOLD/PET results. It is unclear whether the imaging task qualifies as a problem-solving/reasoning task (they measured fluid intelligence separately), so include for full-text review to resolve I2.

Excluded because the task was a simple motor (fist closure) task, not a problem-solving or reasoning task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy subjects as comparison), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task).

Task-based fMRI study using the Raven's Progressive Matrices (a reasoning/problem-solving task); includes non-autistic (healthy) adult participants; reports task-related brain activation results (regional activity and PPI connectivity). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI matrix reasoning test with normative functional activation data from unimpaired (healthy adult) controls and reports task-related activation; thus it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent.

Task-based fMRI study (with DTI) examining mental arithmetic/problem solving in healthy adult participants; reports task-related brain activation and structure-function correlations. All inclusion criteria (I1-I4) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Event-related fMRI study of a nonverbal analogical reasoning (problem-solving) task; reports task-related increases in prefrontal activation. Abstract does not explicitly state participant health status (healthy adults), so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Exclusion: I2 not met — the task is kinesthetic locomotion imagery, not a problem-solving or reasoning task. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy adult controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activations). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based neuroimaging study (fMRI) directly comparing false belief and counterfactual reasoning tasks, reporting task-related brain activation results. Participants performed reasoning/problem-solving tasks; typical neuroimaging sample implies healthy adults. Thus inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health status and other details.
Task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning (problem solving) in humans; includes healthy adult participants and reports task-related brain activation (parametric ROI results).

This is a task-based fMRI study where human bilingual participants performed mental addition (a problem-solving task) and the abstract reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

E2 met: study is a single-case patient study with no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing arithmetic/problem-solving), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no group of healthy adults reported).

Included for full-text review. Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study reporting task-related brain activation (I1, I4). However, it is unclear whether the task qualifies as problem-solving/reasoning (I2) and whether participants are explicitly healthy adults (I3). No exclusion criteria met.

Empirical task-based fMRI study of probabilistic decision-making (a reasoning task) including 28 healthy adult controls and reporting task-related brain activations in relevant regions; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a human WCST task assessing cognitive flexibility/problem-solving (I2). The abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI/PET (I1 unclear), does not confirm inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3 unclear), nor explicitly report task-related activation results (I4 unclear). Because presence of healthy controls and imaging modality/results are uncertain, include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Excluded (E2): participants are episodic drinkers and regular smokers; no healthy adult group is reported. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (does not involve a problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult sample reported).

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in humans performing a hypothesis-testing/category induction task (a form of problem solving/reasoning), includes healthy adult participants (implied typical fMRI sample), and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of relational reasoning (a problem-solving/reasoning task), includes adult participants (ages up to 30), and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI experiment (I1) of deductive reasoning (I2) and describes task-related activations (I4). Participant health/age not specified (I3 uncertain); include for full-text review to confirm healthy adult sample.

Abstract reports two task-based fMRI experiments in college students solving novel and old scientific innovation problems, with reported task-related brain activations (lingual gyrus, precuneus) correlated with behavior. This meets inclusion criteria for task-based imaging, problem-solving task, healthy adult sample, and reported activation. No exclusion criteria identified.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based PET/fMRI study), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task performed), I3 (healthy adult sample not demonstrated), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). The study is a PET scanner/methods validation in humans, not a task-based problem-solving neuroimaging study.

E1 and E2 apply: this is a meta-analysis of diagnostic imaging for colorectal liver metastases (no original task-based human activation data) and does not include healthy adult samples. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET), I2 (problem-solving task), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Therefore exclude from review.

Included for full-text review: the study is a task-based fMRI study, reports task-related brain activation, and includes a healthy adult group (20-year-olds). It is unclear from the abstract whether the mini Ultimatum Game qualifies as a 'problem-solving or reasoning' task (I2), as it is primarily a social decision-making/intentionality task, so full-text review is needed to determine eligibility.

Does not meet I2: the task (stop-change multitasking) is not described as a problem-solving or reasoning task. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task not met), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly stated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) clearly met from abstract.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI (I1), participants performing multirule rule-learning/execution tasks (I2), and task-related activation results (I4). It does not explicitly state that participants are healthy adults (I3 not confirmed), so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

E2 met: study includes only brain tumour patients and no healthy adult sample. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based PET) and I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (task is motor finger/foot movements, not problem-solving/reasoning) and I3 (no healthy adults).
Task-based fMRI study of deductive (problem-solving) reasoning with 12 human volunteers; reports task-related brain activation across phases. Satisfies all inclusion criteria based on abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study that manipulated reasoning demands (deductive vs. abductive) and reports mPFC activation—meets I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state the participant sample are healthy adults (I3 not confirmed). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm healthy adult sample and extract details.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with task-related parietal activations (I1, I4). However, it is unclear whether the number-identification task qualifies as a problem-solving/reasoning task (I2 unclear) and the abstract does not explicitly state inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3 unclear). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine I2 and I3.

Task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating transitive reasoning and number representation; reports task-related activations (anterior intraparietal sulcus, basal ganglia). All inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I3, I4) are clearly met and no exclusion criteria apply.

E1 applies — non-empirical review without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no reported participants performing a problem-solving task), I3 (no original healthy adult sample), I4 (no original task-related activation results).

No task-based fMRI/PET (I1 not met), not a problem-solving/reasoning task (I2 not met), and no task-related brain activation reported (I4 not met). It does include healthy matched controls (I3 met). No exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study with three healthy adult participants reporting task-related activation increases after WM training. However, it's unclear whether a problem-solving/reasoning task was performed during the imaging sessions (the abstract mentions behavioral improvement on a reasoning task but imaging was during WM and baseline tasks). Include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study examining 'making sense' of conversation and appraisal of conversational reasoning, and it reports task-related brain activations (regions involved). This satisfies I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not specify participant population (healthy adults not explicitly stated), so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental calculation (problem-solving) comparing abacus experts and controls. It includes healthy adult participants and reports task-related brain activation results (e.g., parietal, premotor, fusiform activity). No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets I1: task-based fMRI study; I2: participants performed a logical reasoning/problem-solving task; I3: includes healthy control group(s); I4: reports task-related brain activation results (performance-correlated activity). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Includes task-based fMRI (I1) investigating causal reasoning during overt word production, a reasoning/problem-solving-like task (I2), and reports task-related BOLD activations (I4). The abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults, so I3 is not confirmed; include for full-text review to verify sample health. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study sampled children (ages 4–6) and includes no healthy adult participants (E2). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation/effective connectivity). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (task is a magnitude-comparison, not clearly a problem-solving/reasoning task for the review), I3 (no healthy adult sample).

Task-based fMRI study in humans (10 subjects) reporting task-related activation. Includes a calculation task (mental calculation), which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving/reasoning in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria met in the abstract.

EXCLUDE due to E2: sample includes children/adolescents and healthy controls but no healthy adult group. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed a categorical n-back reasoning/executive task), I4 (reports task-related neural activation). Inclusion not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample).

Exclusion IDs met: None. Inclusion IDs met: None. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (study is not task-based PET/fMRI; it examines resting FDG distribution under mild hyperglycemia), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task), I3 (healthy adult sample not demonstrated), I4 (no task-related activation reported). Therefore excluded from the review focused on task-based problem-solving studies.

Task-based fMRI study of adults performing grammatical transformation (a verbal reasoning/problem-solving task). N=18 adults (presumably healthy) and the abstract reports task-related brain activation findings. Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

The abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with 18 right-handed participants performing problem-solving tasks (anagrams and spatial puzzles) and reports task-related brain activation. It appears to involve healthy adult subjects. All inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

E2 met: single-case study of an individual with Asperger syndrome—no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (unclear whether task-based fMRI/PET from abstract), I2 (task-based problem-solving not clearly reported), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (task-related activation results not clearly reported).

Exclusion E2 met: abstract reports fMRI of two expert individuals (one with Asperger's) with no healthy adult sample reported. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (problem-solving/calendar task), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I3 (includes at least one group of healthy adults) is not demonstrated in abstract.

EXCLUDED because the abstract does not report a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I1), includes healthy adult participants (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) are met.

Task-based fMRI study of transitive inference (reasoning/problem-solving) in human participants; reports task-related activation in frontal and parietal regions. No exclusions apparent. All inclusion criteria satisfied.

No evidence the task is a problem-solving or reasoning task (it is a perspective-taking/counting visuospatial task). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (problem-solving/reasoning). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Study is task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4). It is unclear from the abstract whether the tasks constitute problem-solving/reasoning (Story comprehension vs. a serial-arithmetic control), so inclusion criterion I2 is uncertain. Include for full-text review to determine if the math or other task meets the problem-solving criterion.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study where human participants performed difficult moral dilemmas (a reasoning task), and describes task-related brain activation. Healthy adult sample is implied in typical participant description. Meets I1, I2, I4 and likely I3; include for full-text review to confirm participant details.

This is a methodological MRI+FDG-PET study of bone marrow metabolism, not a task-based PET/fMRI study of problem solving. It does not involve problem-solving tasks or report task-related brain activation; a healthy adult sample is not demonstrated. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1, I2, I3 (not demonstrated), I4.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans performing calculation tasks (serial subtraction, basic/complex/abstract calculation) which are problem-solving tasks; includes healthy age-matched control group and reports task-related activations. No exclusion criteria met.

EXCLUDE: study does not involve a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task; study examines empathy for pain/social context).

No problem-solving task and no evidence of healthy adult sample in abstract. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task absent; study focuses on memory), I3 (no clear healthy adult group reported). Therefore exclude from this review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not demonstrated: I2 (participants performing a problem-solving/reasoning task) — mental arithmetic was used as a stressor, not as a targeted problem-solving task relevant to the review objective.

Excluded because the study used EEG (ERP) rather than task-based fMRI or PET, so I1 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (human participants performing a reasoning task) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG components). Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I3 (presence of a healthy adult sample is not specified). No exclusion criteria met (E1/E2).

Task-based fMRI study of visuospatial analogical reasoning in humans that reports task-related brain activation (RLPFC, IFG, inferior parietal cortex). Participants are healthy adults (typical fMRI cognitive study). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Event-related fMRI study (I1) with 14 human volunteers performing a quantitative reasoning/problem-solving task (comparing perimeters) (I2), includes healthy adult volunteers (I3), and reports task-related brain activation findings (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract provides sufficient detail to include for full-text review.

Excluded because this is a systematic review/meta-analysis of FDG-PET in colorectal cancer (E1) and involves cancer patients rather than healthy adults (E2). No task-based fMRI/PET experiments of problem solving are reported (I1 not met), participants are not performing problem-solving/reasoning tasks (I2 not met), no healthy adult sample is included (I3 not met), and no task-related brain activation results for problem solving are reported (I4 not met).

Study uses task-based fMRI, includes healthy control group, and reports task-related activation, but abstract does not clearly indicate the fMRI task was a problem-solving or reasoning task (fMRI used a verbal working memory task). Inclusion for full-text review is appropriate to determine whether the task meets the problem-solving/reasoning criterion.

Excluded because the study used affect-processing tasks, not problem-solving or reasoning tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task not present). No exclusion criteria met.

E2 met: study includes glioma patients, not a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study; diagnostic FET-PET), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adults), I4 (no task-related brain activation results for problem solving).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI adaptation study reporting task-related BOLD responses to non-symbolic proportions (satisfies I1 and I4). The abstract does not explicitly state participant demographics or that the task constituted problem-solving/reasoning, so I2 and I3 are uncertain—full-text review required.

Task-based fMRI study in healthy volunteers requiring them to reason about protagonists' intentions/expectations (theory-of-mind), reporting task-related brain activations for cooperation vs deception. Meets I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (reasoning task), I3 (healthy adults), and I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria apparent.

E2 met: study does not include any healthy adult sample (participants are medication-naïve ADHD boys and matched child controls). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI or PET study; it is resting-state fMRI), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task; resting-state), I3 (no healthy adults), I4 (does not report task-related activation results).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI or PET study), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task), I3 (no evidence of healthy adult participants), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Task-based fMRI in healthy adult volunteers reporting task-related brain activation during verbal fluency and N-back working memory. However, the tasks are executive/working memory rather than explicitly described as problem-solving or reasoning, so I2 is uncertain. Include for full-text review to determine whether tasks meet the review's problem-solving/reasoning requirement.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based event-related fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activations). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (does not involve a problem-solving or reasoning task; it assesses praxis/gesture planning), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly stated in abstract). Therefore excluded for not meeting the review’s problem-solving task criterion.

E2 met: study images cancer patients with FDG-PET/CT for tumor staging and does not include healthy adult participants. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants performing a mental-state decoding (reasoning) task and reports task-related brain activation. While 'mental state decoding' may be narrower than typical problem-solving tasks, it fits the review's ‘reasoning’ criterion, so include for full-text review.

PET study mapping brain activation during the PASAT (meets I1 and I4). The PASAT involves arithmetic but abstract does not explicitly confirm it as a problem-solving/reasoning task per inclusion I2 nor explicitly state participants were healthy adults (I3). No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to clarify I2 and I3.

Abstract describes an event-related fMRI study with human participants performing a problem-solving/reasoning task (mental arithmetic with working memory integration), reports task-related brain activation, and likely involves healthy adult participants; include for full-text review to confirm participant health details.

Task-based fMRI study investigating logical reasoning/pragmatic processing using narrative tasks; participants performed reasoning/inference tasks; reports brain activation and connectivity results. Sample appears to be healthy adult participants. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria evident from abstract.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related brain activation for autobiographical memory, prospection, and theory-of-mind reasoning (meets I1, I2, I4). The abstract does not explicitly state the sample were healthy adults (I3 unclear). Include for full-text review to confirm presence of healthy adult participants and extract details.

Exclusion E2 met: study involves patients with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma, not a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based PET/fMRI study; diagnostic imaging), I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported).

Excluded: meets E2 (no healthy adult sample—study of prostate cancer patients). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based PET/fMRI study; diagnostic imaging), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported).

Abstract reports human mental-arithmetic task and presents task-related brain activation results, satisfying I2 and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state use of fMRI/PET (I1) or specify healthy adult sample (I3), so full-text review is needed to confirm those criteria.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (participants did recognition/episodic memory tasks, not problem-solving or reasoning). Therefore excluded for not addressing problem-solving tasks.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI activation (frontoparietal control network) during moral judgment, a form of controlled reasoning (satisfies I1, I2, I4). The abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults, so I3 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria clearly met. Recommend full-text review to confirm participant health and task details.

Excluded due to E2: study sample consists of patients with cervical compressive myelopathy and does not include a healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based PET/fMRI study), I2 (no problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult participants), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

EXCLUDED because the study does not involve a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (participants performed memory/match-detection judgments, not a problem-solving or reasoning task).

Task-based fMRI study (I1) with 106 healthy adult participants (I3) performing fluid reasoning and perceptual speed tasks (I2). The abstract reports task-related neural activation and topographic similarity results (I4). No exclusion criteria met; abstract provides clear evidence for all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Excluded because the study includes only patients with temporal lobe epilepsy and has no healthy adult sample (E2). It meets I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related activations). It does NOT meet I2 (task is language/verbal fluency, not problem-solving/reasoning) and I3 (no healthy adult group).

Excluded because the study used EEG/ERP network analysis rather than task-based fMRI or PET (I1 not met). The abstract describes moral decision-making tasks (I2) and reports task-related brain connectivity/activation results (I4). The abstract does not state inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are clearly met.

Exclusion criteria met: E1 and E2. The abstract is a methodological/technical discussion of imaging for radiotherapy (appears non-empirical) and does not report original human PET/fMRI task data or any problem-solving tasks. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I3, I4.

Excluded because the study used an event-related oddball task (not a problem-solving or reasoning task), so I2 is not met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related fMRI analysis/results). Inclusion not met or not demonstrated: I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task not present) and I3 (healthy adult sample not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) clearly met.

Excluded: the study is a small-animal preclinical imaging study of cancer metastasis, not a task-based human PET/fMRI investigation. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (no healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based human PET/fMRI), I2 (no human problem-solving task), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported).

Task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants reporting task-related brain activation. However, abstract does not clearly indicate whether the primary tasks constitute 'problem solving'—emotional/cognitive perspective-taking may not meet the review's problem-solving focus, though a control involved inferential reasoning. Inclusion criteria I1, I3, and I4 are met; I2 is unclear. Include for full-text review to resolve whether tasks meet the problem-solving/reasoning requirement.

Exclude: Abstract describes passive viewing of goal-directed actions (not a problem-solving or reasoning task — I2 not met) and does not specify a healthy adult sample (I3 not demonstrated). It is a task-based fMRI study reporting activation (I1 and I4 met). No exclusion criteria clearly met (none).

Excluded because the abstract describes a methodological fMRI reliability study, not a study of problem-solving or reasoning tasks (I2 not met). The paper is task-based fMRI (I1) and reports task-related activation results (I4). Inclusion of healthy adult participants is not demonstrated in the abstract (I3 not shown). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related BOLD activation (meets I1 and I4). Participants performed implicit false-belief processing (a reasoning/theory-of-mind task), so I2 appears satisfied. The abstract does not specify whether participants were healthy adults (I3 not demonstrated); therefore include for full-text review to confirm sample health/age.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (includes healthy adult controls). Inclusion NOT met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study; it's resting-state), I2 (participants did not perform a problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (reports resting-state functional connectivity, not task-related activation). Therefore exclude based on unmet inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related activation for participants identifying how and why actions were performed, which constitutes a reasoning task. The abstract does not explicitly state sample health status, so include for full-text review to confirm healthy adult sample.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study—it's a PET methods/CBF quantification paper), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task reported), I3 (healthy adult status not specified), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

Exclusion E2 met: title/abstract indicate study of a parietal lesion (patient sample), not healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (no evidence of task-based fMRI/PET), I2 (no clear problem-solving/reasoning task reported), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Exclude based on absence of healthy adult sample and insufficient abstract evidence.

Exclusion E2: study does not include any healthy adult participants. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI reported) and I4 (task-related brain activation results reported). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participants performing a problem-solving/reasoning task) and I3 (includes at least one group of healthy adults).

E2 met: study includes only children (no healthy adult sample). No inclusion criteria met: I1 (not task-based fMRI/PET; DTI/structural), I2 (not a problem-solving/reasoning task; memory span tests only), I3 (no healthy adults), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported). Therefore excluded.

E2 met: study examines NSCLC patients (clinical imaging), not healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI with task-related brain activation and includes adult participants (ages 4–37). However, the task involves moral judgment/sensitivity rather than an explicit problem-solving paradigm, so relevance to ‘problem solving’ is uncertain from the abstract; full-text review recommended.

Excluded for E2: sample consists of subjects with history of alcoholism and no healthy adult sample is reported. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no evidence this is a task-based PET study), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task described), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

EXCLUDED because the task is social-cognition/theory-of-mind judgments about well-known individuals, not a problem-solving or reasoning task (fails I2). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (E2 not applicable).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — the task is artificial grammar learning/grammaticality judgment (implicit learning/memory), not a problem-solving or reasoning task, so it does not address the review objective.

Task-based fMRI study of everyday moral reasoning (decision task) with twelve healthy subjects that reports task-related brain activation results. This satisfies I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of transitive inference (a reasoning/problem-solving task) in human participants, reports task-related brain activation (RLPFC and hippocampus), and appears to include healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (includes healthy adults). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study — resting-state fMRI), I2 (participants not performing a problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (no task-related activation reported). Excluded because the study uses resting-state ICA, not task-based problem-solving imaging (high confidence).

Abstract does not provide sufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria: it appears to study Parkinson’s disease and dopaminergic dysfunction but does not specify whether task-based fMRI/PET was used for a problem-solving task or whether healthy adults were included. Exclusion criteria are not clearly met from the abstract alone. Recommend full-text review to determine eligibility.

Task-based fMRI study in humans performing a fluid analogy task (problem solving/reasoning) with healthy adult participants; reports task-related BOLD activation results. Abstract satisfies all inclusion criteria for full-text review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that includes tasks tapping fluid reasoning/problem-solving (one of the reference abilities) and reports task-related brain activation and multivariate activation results. All inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

EXCLUDED because the study is a PET ligand/kinetics methods paper, not a task-based activation study. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1, E2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study), I2 (no problem-solving or reasoning task), I4 (no task-related activation results). I3 (healthy adult sample) is not demonstrated in abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants, appears to involve healthy adult subjects, and reports task-related brain activations. It is unclear from the abstract whether the Waterloo Gestalt Closure Task is considered a problem-solving/reasoning task (I2 not clearly demonstrated). Include for full-text review to confirm whether the task meets the problem-solving criterion.

No. The study uses task-based fMRI of auditory categorization, not a problem-solving or reasoning task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 (does not involve a problem-solving/reasoning task), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly stated in abstract).

Excluding: study uses task-based fMRI of motor planning/pantomime, not a problem-solving or reasoning task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1, E2 not met).

E2: study involves patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, not healthy adults. It is not a task-based fMRI or PET problem-solving study. Inclusion criteria met: none. This is a task-based fMRI study with 18 healthy adult participants and reports task-related brain activations. Because inclusion on that criterion (I2) is uncertain from the abstract, include for full-text review.

Study used resting-state fMRI (rsfc-MRI), not a task-based fMRI or PET paradigm, and participants were not reported performing a problem-solving/reasoning task; no task-evoked activation results are reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET), I2 (problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (task-related brain activation). Study is a task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants and reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not clearly indicate the task is a problem-solving or reasoning task relevant to the review (I2 not demonstrated); include for full-text review to resolve.

Exclusion based on abstract: study used resting-state fMRI (no task). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (healthy adults). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI/PET), I2 (participants performing a problem-solving/reasoning task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).
